title: How do you use the 3Cs to get started on an open case question?
description: A quick strategic scan when you need a starting structure for an open question.
hook: The 3Cs (company, customers and competitors) is one of the oldest tools in strategy, and still one of the most useful for getting your bearings on a new problem. Here is how to use it without sounding like a textbook.
body:
When it helps

A quick strategic scan when you need a starting structure for an open question.

The checklist

Customers

  • Who they are
  • What they need
  • How they buy

Company

  • Strengths and gaps
  • Costs and capacity
  • Brand

Competitors

  • Who they are
  • Their share and moves
  • Their advantages

An example

A family-run bakery is asked whether to open a second shop. Customers: who buys from them today, and is there a similar crowd in the new area? Company: can the owners run two shops, and is the bakery big enough to supply both? Competitors: who already sells bread and cakes near the new site, and how good are they? Three short questions, and you have a sensible first view.

How it sounds in an interview

To get my bearings, I'd like to look at three things: the customers, the company itself, and the competition. I'll start with customers, since everything depends on whether there is demand.
outro: The The 3Cs checklist is also on the free frameworks page. Next in this topic: How do you use Porter's five forces to judge an industry in a case?
